name: First shot at Santa Mesa
summary: Pvt. William Grayson of the 1st Nebraska, on picket near Santa Mesa, fires on a Filipino soldier who will not halt or answer his challenge; the Filipino lines near Santa Mesa open fire. Otis puts the start of the battle at half past eight.
playback_text: Private William Grayson of the 1st Nebraska, on picket near Santa Mesa, fires on one Filipino soldier who will not halt or answer his challenge, and the lines open fire. The battle begins at 20:30.

name: Firing along the north front through the night
summary: An exchange of fire from the Pasig to the Lico road, about two miles, with occasional shots at Paco and towards Caloocan. Heavy firing at midnight and at 4 a.m. Anderson is told at midnight to hold, not attack.
playback_text: Fire is exchanged along the north front from the Pasig to the Lico road; heavy at midnight and at 04:00. South of the Pasig, Anderson is told to hold and not attack.

name: Stotsenburg takes Blockhouses 6 and 7
summary: The 1st Nebraska attacks early in the morning and drives the Filipinos from the blockhouses in its front.
playback_text: The 1st Nebraska attacks at first light and takes Blockhouses 6 and 7.

name: Anderson allowed to attack
summary: Permission for the First Division to attack is given at 7:45 a.m., with a caution to watch its flanks and the monitor Monadnock's fire.
playback_text: Anderson's division south of the Pasig is allowed to attack. King swings his brigade left towards the Pasig.

name: Nebraskans cross the San Juan bridge
summary: MacArthur reports Stotsenburg crossing the San Juan River at the bridge at 11:20; the Nebraskans and a Tennessee battalion take the powder magazine and the reservoir (El Deposito).
playback_text: The Nebraskans cross the San Juan River at the bridge and take the powder magazine and the reservoir, El Deposito.

name: King takes Santa Ana
summary: Anderson reports from Battery Knoll at 12:30 that King has taken Santa Ana with 200 prisoners; Filipinos trying to cross the Pasig are drowned. Colonel Smith's Californians are entering San Pedro Macati.
playback_text: King's brigade takes Santa Ana; many Filipinos drown trying to cross the Pasig. The Californians enter San Pedro Macati.

name: Ovenshine takes Pasay
summary: Ovenshine swings part of his line left, routs the Filipinos in front of Murphy and places his line on the Pasay road; Pasay is taken without resistance.
playback_text: Ovenshine swings left, clears the ground in front of the centre and takes Pasay without resistance.

name: Close of the day
summary: The new line: on the south the road from Pasay to San Pedro Macati; on the north the reservoir, San Juan del Monte and all the blockhouses, and MacArthur's line from opposite San Pedro Macati to the bay.
playback_text: The battle ends about 17:00. The Americans hold the road from Pasay to San Pedro Macati in the south, and the reservoir, San Juan del Monte and the blockhouses in the north.

name: War begins at Manila
summary: Fighting breaks out around Manila on the evening of 4 February; by the next evening the Eighth Army Corps has driven the Filipino army from its lines around the city.
playback_text: The war begins at Manila on the evening of 4 February. The Manila playback follows these two days hour by hour.

name: Caloocan taken
summary: MacArthur swings his left onto Caloocan, driving off a Filipino force put at 4,000.
playback_text: MacArthur's division takes Caloocan, the railway town north of Manila.

name: The line of the Pasig
summary: Wheaton's provisional brigade clears Pasig, Pateros and Taguig between 10 and 17 March, cutting the Filipino forces north of Manila off from those south of it. Lawton takes over the First Division.
playback_text: Wheaton clears the Pasig River to the lake, cutting the Filipino forces north of Manila from those to the south. Lawton arrives and takes the First Division.

name: Malolos falls
summary: MacArthur's division, advancing from 25 March, enters Malolos, the capital of the Republic, which its army has set on fire. The government has gone.
playback_text: After a week's advance up the railway MacArthur enters Malolos, the Republic's capital, burning and empty. The Filipino army falls back to Calumpit.

name: Lawton takes Santa Cruz
summary: Lawton crosses Laguna de Bay with 1,500 men and takes Santa Cruz; he is back in Manila on the 17th.
playback_text: Lawton crosses Laguna de Bay and takes Santa Cruz, then returns to Manila.

name: Calumpit: the Rio Grande crossed
summary: MacArthur forces the Bagbag and the Rio Grande at Calumpit against Luna's army; Lawton, marching round by Norzagaray, is closing on Baliuag.
playback_text: MacArthur's men cross the Rio Grande at Calumpit under the fire of the Utah guns. Lawton's column is working round the Filipino left by Norzagaray.

name: San Fernando
summary: MacArthur takes San Fernando and is halted there; Lawton holds Baliuag.
playback_text: MacArthur takes San Fernando and is ordered to stop there. His division will hold it through the rains.

name: San Isidro
summary: Lawton seizes San Isidro, the Republic's capital since Malolos. Aguinaldo and his cabinet retire to Cabanatuan; Luna's army falls back on Tarlac. The rains then end the campaign.
playback_text: Lawton seizes San Isidro. The Republic's government retires to Cabanatuan and its army to Tarlac. The rains end the spring campaign; San Isidro is given up.

name: Angeles
summary: In August MacArthur pushes his line ten miles up the railway to Angeles. The day is not in the sources read.
playback_text: During August MacArthur moves up the railway to Angeles, which becomes his headquarters.

name: San Isidro retaken
summary: Lawton's column, with Young's cavalry leading, crosses at Arayat on 17 October and retakes San Isidro on the 20th.
playback_text: The fall campaign opens: Lawton's column, Young's cavalry leading, retakes San Isidro. The plan is three columns closing on the Filipino army: Lawton up the Rio Grande, MacArthur up the railway, Wheaton by sea to Lingayen Gulf.

name: Wheaton lands at San Fabian
summary: Wheaton's expedition lands at San Fabian on Lingayen Gulf, behind the Filipino army. MacArthur has been advancing from Angeles since the 5th; Young leaves Cabanatuan for the north.
playback_text: Wheaton lands at San Fabian on Lingayen Gulf, across the Filipino army's way north. MacArthur is advancing up the railway; Young's cavalry heads for the mountain trails.

name: San Jacinto
summary: Wheaton's 33rd Infantry routs Manuel Tinio's brigade of about 1,200 near San Jacinto, the force that was to have escorted Aguinaldo north; 134 Filipino dead.
playback_text: Wheaton's 33rd Infantry routs Manuel Tinio's brigade of about 1,200 at San Jacinto, dug in behind flooded rice fields; 134 of its men are killed. It was the force that was to have escorted Aguinaldo north.

name: Tarlac falls; Aguinaldo goes north
summary: MacArthur's advance enters Tarlac on the evening of the 12th and finds it nearly empty. At Bayambang, on the 12th or 13th, Aguinaldo and his generals agree to break the army up into guerrilla bands; he leaves for the north.
playback_text: MacArthur enters Tarlac, the Republic's capital, on the 12th. At Bayambang Aguinaldo and his generals decide to disband the army into guerrilla bands, and he sets out north with a small escort.

name: Young takes San Fernando de la Union
summary: Young, following Aguinaldo through Pozorrubio, Rosario and Tubao, forces the Aringay River on the 19th and takes San Fernando on the 20th. Aguinaldo sleeps that night at Balaoan, a day ahead.
playback_text: Young's handful of cavalry and Macabebe scouts reach the coast and take San Fernando de la Union. Aguinaldo is a day ahead of them on the coast road.

name: Navy lands at Vigan
summary: Warships shell the trenches at Vigan and land 200 men, who occupy the town.
playback_text: A Navy landing party takes Vigan, ahead of Young. (Otis's report says the 24th; an officer on the spot says the morning of the 26th.)

name: Tirad Pass
summary: March's battalion of the 33rd Infantry carries Tirad Pass, held by Aguinaldo's rear guard under Gregorio del Pilar, who is killed. Aguinaldo leaves Cervantes that night.
playback_text: March's battalion carries Tirad Pass, where Gregorio del Pilar and Aguinaldo's rear guard die holding it. Aguinaldo leaves Cervantes that night for the mountains.

name: Young at Vigan
summary: Young beats Tinio in the pass east of Narvacan on the 4th and reaches Vigan on the 5th. March has passed Cervantes for Cayan; Aguinaldo has gone into the mountains beyond it.
playback_text: Young reaches Vigan the day after Tangadan. Aguinaldo has disappeared into the mountains; the sources read do not follow him further.

name: Cagayan surrenders
summary: Word reaches Manila that the province of Cagayan has surrendered to a Navy force landed at Aparri; Batchelor's battalion, marching down the valley from Bayombong, is nearing the town.
playback_text: The Cagayan valley surrenders to a Navy force at Aparri, as Batchelor's battalion comes down the river from Bayombong. The playback ends here.

name: The advance on Malolos begins
summary: MacArthur's column marches at dawn: Hale's brigade by San Francisco del Monte to Novaliches, H. G. Otis's to the Tulihan River below it, to turn the Filipino left, while Wheaton's brigade drives the Filipino line from Caloocan back across the river.
playback_text: MacArthur's division marches at dawn to turn the Filipino left by Novaliches, while Wheaton's brigade attacks up the railway from Caloocan. Zoom in on Manila to see the brigades.

name: Laoag
summary: The Wheeling lands a force at Laoag on the 10th, where some 1,500 Spanish prisoners are found. Young follows by sea in the Samar on the 11th to direct the pursuit of Tinio, who holds the American prisoners.
playback_text: The Navy lands a force at Laoag, and Young follows from Vigan by sea in the gunboat Samar. His columns are in the mountains after Tinio, who holds the American prisoners.

name: The Cavite expedition
summary: Schwan's column and a Marine battalion, with warships firing in support, break through at Kawit and Noveleta; Lawton joins them and they enter San Francisco de Malabon on the 10th. The expedition costs 2 dead and 23 wounded; Otis then pulls back to the Bacoor-Imus line.
playback_text: South of Manila, Schwan's column and a Marine battalion clear Kawit and Noveleta under the guns of the warships, and with Lawton enter San Francisco de Malabon on the 10th. Then Otis pulls back to the Bacoor-Imus line and turns north.

name: Attack on Angeles
summary: Before dawn the Filipino army attacks the Angeles outposts along miles of the line; it is beaten off with heavy loss.
playback_text: Before dawn the Filipino army attacks the Angeles outposts along miles of the line. It is beaten off with heavy loss, a costly failure that further demoralizes it.

name: Wheeler at the Paruao
summary: In front of Bamban, Wheeler is sent to hold the defenders while other units flank them; he charges across the Paruao River instead and drives them back miles.
playback_text: In front of Bamban, Wheeler's brigade is told to hold the defenders while others flank them. He charges across the Paruao River instead and drives them back miles; MacArthur sends him to the rear.

name: Swigert at Pozorrubio
summary: Swigert's squadron of the 3rd Cavalry strikes Aguinaldo's rear guard outside Pozorrubio late on the 14th and captures his mother and son; by morning Aguinaldo has gone.
playback_text: Late on the 14th Swigert's cavalry strikes Aguinaldo's rear guard outside Pozorrubio and captures his mother and son. Swigert halts for the night; by morning Aguinaldo has turned north-west over the mountains.

name: Mangatarem
summary: Fowler's company of the 33rd attacks Alejandrino's 500 to 1,000 at Mangatarem and, seeming a larger force, drives them out; the 36th joins it on the 26th, linking Wheaton and MacArthur.
playback_text: One company of the 33rd under Fowler attacks Alejandrino's 500 to 1,000 at Mangatarem. Bugle calls and shifting formations make it seem larger; the defenders leave guns, stores and Spanish prisoners. On the 26th the 36th joins it.

name: Vigan attacked
summary: Before dawn about 400 of Tinio's men come down the Abra River by boat and attack Vigan; Company B and the sick of the 33rd, about 120, fire 15,000 rounds and hold the plaza until daylight.
playback_text: Before dawn about 400 of Tinio's men come down the Abra River by boat into Vigan, with bolomen hidden in the cathedral. About 120 men of the 33rd hold the plaza in close fighting; by daylight the attackers have melted away.

name: Tangadan Pass
summary: With barely 150 men Young attacks about 700 under Juan and Blas Villamor in Tangadan Pass; Hare's 33rd, which has marched up the coast, comes out on the flanks, and the Villamors withdraw in good order when their ammunition runs out.
playback_text: East of Narvacan, Young with barely 150 men attacks about 700 under the cousins Juan and Blas Villamor. Hare's 33rd, marching up the coast, climbs onto the flanks; the Villamors withdraw in good order when their ammunition runs out.

name: Howze catches Tinio
summary: In Abra, Howze's battalion catches Tinio's brigade after three escaped prisoners show the way; a three-hour running fight ends it as a fighting force.
playback_text: In Abra three escaped prisoners lead Howze's battalion to Tinio's brigade. In a three-hour running fight it loses 200 rifles, 60,000 rounds and most of its arsenal, and is finished as a fighting force.
